speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) since 2022, how many inpatient hospice patients have sought ElderShield claims; (b) of these, how many claims have been approved; (c) what is the median time taken from application to the commencement of payout; (d) how many have been approved through (i) severe disability assessor review by a visiting assessor and (ii) resident assessment forms submitted by the inpatient hospices, respectively; and (d) whether the claims of patients with severely limited life expectancy in inpatient hospices can be expedited.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Resident Assessment Form is an assessment tool that is typically used in nursing homes and is not commonly used in inpatient hospices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) proactively looks out for claims applications from patients with limited life expectancy and prioritises the processing of their claims applications.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My Clementi resident was terminally ill, admitted to an inpatient hospice.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Her family shared they had difficulty getting an assessor to go to the inpatient hospice.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Eventually, the AIC asked if the hospice could arrange a Resident Assessment Form.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But then, the family were told there needed to be two assessments done six months apart.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But six months is a very long time for a terminally ill patient in a hospice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We thank Dr Tan for raising a very important issue so that we can enhance our claims processes for patients with limited life expectancy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: More broadly, AIC will proactively look up for claims from patients with limited life expectancies and prioritise processing of their applications.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are also exploring the possibility of allowing tele-assessments to further improve accessibility of severe disability accessors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we hope that in doing all these efforts, the concerns raised by Dr Tan will be addressed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
